summary: Mundus Journalism is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master's in journalism, media and globalisation. You start at Aarhus University in Denmark and spend the second year in Amsterdam, London, Munich or Prague. The programme expects to give 10 to 15 scholarships, open to every nationality, with free tuition and €1,400 a month. Applications close on 10 January 2027 at 13:00 CET.
meta_title: Mundus Journalism 2027: Erasmus Mundus journalism scholarship
meta_description: Mundus Journalism pays tuition and €1,400 a month for a two-year master's from Aarhus to Amsterdam, London, Munich or Prague. Apply by 10 January 2027.
covers: A full waiver of tuition fees for both years. Self-funded non-EU students pay €9,000 for the first year and €12,000 for the second.
€1,400 a month for up to 24 months.
eligibility: A bachelor's degree of at least three years of full-time study, with above-average grades. Final-year students can apply and send proof by 1 August.
At least three months of documented full-time journalistic work; internships and unpaid work count.
English at C1 unless you are a native speaker. Exemptions depend on the second-year university and are mostly country-based; Ghana and Nigeria are not named.
how_to_apply: Apply online between 1 November 2026 and 10 January 2027 at 13:00 CET.

Combine into one PDF, in order: the signed application form, a CV of up to two pages, transcripts and certificates, an employer statement with three work samples, your English evidence, and two signed references (one academic, one professional).
Upload a copy of your passport separately.
Results come out on 1 March 2027, and offers must be accepted by 15 March.
watch_out: Holders of a two-year master's after a three-year bachelor's, and past Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders, cannot get a scholarship.
Plan for an English test such as IELTS if your second-year choice does not exempt you.
Self-funded second-year students may receive an Erasmus+ stipend of up to €6,000, which is separate from the scholarship.
documents: Transcripts and certificates, translated if not in English
Employer statement and three work samples
Two signed references, one academic and one professional

faq.q: When is the Mundus Journalism deadline?
faq.a: 10 January 2027 at 13:00 CET. Applications opened on 1 November 2026.
Yes: at least three months of documented full-time journalistic work. Internships and unpaid work count.

faq.q: How many Mundus Journalism scholarships are there?
faq.a: The programme expects to offer 10 to 15 Erasmus Mundus scholarships for 2027–2029.
